identityReview: German former foreign minister and former president of the 80th General Assembly, now Columbia SIPA professor of professional practice and MPA faculty co-director. Exact birth date is supported by parliamentary records; expanded name is corroborated by the indexed official 2025 election roster. No current Bundestag mandate, ministerial role or UN presidency is inferred from stale descriptions. Vordiplom is not represented as a bachelor’s degree and unfinished doctoral work is not a doctorate.
lifeStatusEvidence: CIRSD’s read retrospective dated 7 October 2026 records a completed Columbia discussion, without a separate event date. A later indexed Columbia retrospective explicitly reports the 26 October Uppsala lecture and medal; its full article was inaccessible. The October 19 Uppsala advance notice and November 10 Toronto event listing are not used alone as proof of attendance. No audiovisual inspection is claimed.

sourceReview.accessMethod: Read Bundestag current and archived biographies, Columbia faculty profile and appointment release, UN-in-India biography, Foreign Office inaugural report and policy speech, ARD policy reporting, IISD process account, CIRSD discussion retrospective, SRF leadership report and Commons license/crop metadata. UN 81st-session handover and Columbia lecture retrospective were available as explicit indexed extracts only.
corrections: Read Bundestag current biographical record and editorial departure note. Birth is 15 December 1980 in Hanover. Editorial note states resignation submitted 15 June 2025 and membership ended with 30 June 2025; this overrides the stale self-reported line saying member since 2013 to today. Hamburg qualification is Vordiplom, London is LL.M.; doctoral project explicitly unfinished. Personal family and religious details are not reproduced.

Read the archived 19th-term Bundestag biography. It identifies London studies in 2004–2005, party leadership from 27 January 2018, Bundestag membership from October 2013 and climate-policy spokesperson role in 2013–2017. Treat the page as historical and member-supplied, not a current appointment record. Current page lists doctoral admission in 2008 while archive describes research in 2009–2013; no exact doctoral start date is asserted.

Read Columbia SIPA current faculty profile. It confirms Professor of Professional Practice and Faculty Co-Director, MPA in Global Leadership. Its erroneous ministerial dates December 2001–May 2005 are rejected against the Foreign Office and UN records. Its historical presidency language does not establish current UN office. Do not infer tenure status, a completed PhD, or sole personal authorship of government policies from the title or promotional biography.

Read Columbia faculty announcement, explicitly posted 25 August 2026. Baerbock joins in autumn as professor of professional practice and MPA faculty co-director; announcement date is not first working or teaching day. Its description of the UN presidency as already past is not used to shorten her term. The neighbouring biographies and degrees belong to other appointees.

Read UN press release hosted by the UN in India, dated 10 September 2025. It confirms election on 2 June 2025, September 2025–September 2026 session, German foreign-minister service December 2021–May 2025 and parliamentary service through June 2025. Its loose Hamburg undergraduate-degree wording is not converted into a bachelor’s degree: the Bundestag specifies Vordiplom. Election and session opening are separate.

Read explicit indexed primary-source extracts of the 81st General Assembly secretary-general selection page: Baerbock conducted the process until 8 September 2026 and a town hall was held on 23 July. Direct page access returned 403. The exact handover date is therefore labelled as indexed evidence in the dossier, corroborated by indexed 80th-session records and later biographies describing her as former president. No full-page read is claimed.

Read Foreign Office report dated 8 December 2021 stating the actual handover from Heiko Maas and Germany’s first female foreign minister taking office. This corrects Columbia’s historical date typo. Future travel plans in the article are not presented as already completed visits.

Read Foreign Office speech presenting feminist foreign policy guidelines on 1 March 2023. Rights, representation and resources are policy priorities, not independently verified outcomes. The speech credits ministry colleagues and distinguishes the Development Ministry’s policy presented with Svenja Schulze. Numerical forecasts and claims about peace-agreement survival are not reproduced as validated findings.

Read ARD Tagesschau policy explanation and criticism passages. Kristina Lunz of the Centre for Feminist Foreign Policy supported a new approach but questioned consistency with rearmament and demanded matching investment in human security. This is attributed criticism, not an adjudicated finding. Separate foreign-policy guidelines from Schulze’s development policy; do not adopt the article’s quoted court-history claim without independent verification.

Read IISD SDG Knowledge Hub account of candidate dialogues and the completed 23 July 2026 town hall. It explains that the Assembly appoints the Secretary-General on Security Council recommendation. The president’s convening role is distinct from personal power to appoint or from herself holding the Secretary-General office. Future events and candidate status at the article’s earlier cutoff are not carried forward as November facts.

Read CIRSD account dated 7 October 2026, describing a completed Columbia discussion with Vuk Jeremić. This is retrospective evidence of participation, not an advance event listing. The exact discussion date is not separately stated; October 7 is treated as report date. His former candidacy is not Baerbock’s.

Read the explicit search-indexed Columbia retrospective stating that she delivered the annual Dag Hammarskjöld Lecture at Uppsala on 26 October 2026 and received its medal. Direct article opens were inaccessible, so both public text and review disclose indexed-only access. The Uppsala university advance press release independently names the event and organisers but does not itself prove attendance. Do not confuse this university/foundation lecture medal with the UN peacekeeping medal or Hammarskjöld’s Nobel award.

Read SRF report of 27 January 2018 confirming that the party congress elected both Annalena Baerbock and Robert Habeck. Preserve joint leadership and do not imply that the party position itself was a federal government office. Service through 2022 is separately supported by Bundestag and UN records.

Search extract identifies her as LLM alumna and graduation in 2005. PDF open timed out; not claimed as a full magazine read.
Indexed official schedule gives 9 September 2025–8 September 2026 session; direct open returned 403.
Search excerpt for 10 November 2026 event; not treated as completed attendance evidence.
Read indexed official elected-candidate roster entry naming Baerbock, Annalena Charlotte Alma. Not claimed as a full roster inspection.

sourceReview.limits: Two adopted recent primary records were available only through indexed extracts, explicitly identified in display text. Exact university first teaching day and CIRSD event day were not established. No complete image download or visual inspection. Review is selective and does not certify all policy outcomes or every statement in the underlying institutional biographies.

translationReview.scope: 32 display fields in each of seven foreign languages checked against Chinese and English. Preserve former versus current posts, joint party and academic leadership, Vordiplom versus LL.M. versus unfinished doctorate, resignation submission versus effective departure, appointment announcement versus teaching date, election versus session dates, indexed-source limitations and attributed policy criticism. No confusion between Assembly president and Secretary-General.
